name: AD ACL Abuse Decision Tree (I have X right -> do Y)
command: # map a BloodHound ACL edge to its abuse; see steps below
description: Master reference: given an ACL edge from BloodHound (GenericAll, GenericWrite, WriteDACL, WriteOwner, ForceChangePassword, AddMember, AddKeyCredentialLink, etc.), which attack to run and which card covers it. Start here after BloodHound flags an outbound control edge.
source: HTB Fluffy engagement; BloodHound ACL abuse
notes:
=== ACL EDGE -> ATTACK -> CARD ===

GenericAll (user):
  - Shadow Credentials (stealth)          -> ad-shadow-credentials
  - ForceChangePassword (loud)            -> ad-force-change-password
  - Targeted Kerberoast (set SPN)         -> ad-targeted-kerberoast

GenericAll / GenericWrite (computer):
  - Shadow Credentials                    -> ad-shadow-credentials
  - RBCD (msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOf...) -> ad-impacket-rbcd

GenericAll / GenericWrite / AddMember (group):
  - Add self to the group (re-auth!)      -> ad-genericall-group

GenericWrite (user, no SPN):
  - Targeted Kerberoast                   -> ad-targeted-kerberoast
  - Shadow Credentials                    -> ad-shadow-credentials

ForceChangePassword (user):
  - Reset the password (loud)             -> ad-force-change-password

WriteDACL (object / domain):
  - Grant self DCSync, then DCSync        -> ad-writedacl-linux
  - Grant self GenericAll, then above

WriteOwner (object):
  - Set self as owner -> WriteDACL -> as above (WriteOwner then WriteDACL then abuse)

WriteProperty msDS-KeyCredentialLink:
  - Shadow Credentials                    -> ad-shadow-credentials

WriteProperty servicePrincipalName (user):
  - Targeted Kerberoast                   -> ad-targeted-kerberoast

WriteProperty msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity (computer):
  - RBCD                                  -> ad-impacket-rbcd

AllowedToDelegate / control of a CA-managing account:
  - ADCS ESC1 (enrollee SAN)              -> ad-esc1-certipy-linux
  - ADCS ESC16 (CA drops SID extension)   -> ad-esc16-upn-manipulation

=== ALWAYS ===
  - Fix clock skew before any Kerberos/PKINIT step -> ad-faketime-kerberos
  - Re-authenticate after group changes (membership is baked into your ticket).
  - Clean up (remove SPNs, key credentials, ACEs, added members) to reduce IOCs.

=== RULE OF THUMB ===
  Write over a user with a writable msDS-KeyCredentialLink -> prefer Shadow Credentials
  (stealthy, reversible) over ForceChangePassword (loud, disruptive).
